title: Follow the Herd: A Data-Driven Approach for Actionable Recourse
abstract: arXiv:2610.36580v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As machine learning systems make increasingly greater decisions about people's lives, it is critical to provide users with actionable recourse about how they can achieve their desired outcomes. This problem is currently tackled by relying on expensive human supervision which involves hand-designing a cost function before searching for low-cost actions that achieve the desired outcome. In this paper, we propose \textit{``Data-Driven Action Recourse"} (DDAR), the first approach for providing action recourse without requiring costly supervision from humans about action costs. We build upon the notion that highly likely trajectories in the historical user data should be associated with lower costs. With this, DDAR first builds a dynamics model of historical user trajectories. Under this model, it then searches for trajectories that achieve the desired outcome. translated_title: 随大流：一种数据驱动的可行动补救方法
translated_abstract: 随着机器学习系统对人们的生活做出越来越重大的决策，为用户提供关于如何实现其期望结果的可行补救建议变得至关重要。目前，这一问题依赖于昂贵的人工监督来解决，即在搜索能够实现期望结果的低成本行动之前，需要人工手工设计成本函数。在本文中，我们提出了“数据驱动行动补救”（DDAR），这是首个无需人类提供关于行动成本的昂贵监督即可提供行动补救的方法。我们的方法基于这样一种理念：历史用户数据中高概率出现的轨迹应与较低的成本相关联。基于此，DDAR首先对历史用户轨迹建立动力学模型，然后在该模型下搜索能够实现期望结果的轨迹。在实验中，我们发现这种简单的方法能够推荐合理且可行的行动补救方案。
tldr: 本文提出首个无需人工设计行动成本函数的数据驱动行动补救方法DDAR，通过学习历史用户轨迹的动力学模型，搜索高概率且能实现期望结果的低成本行动路径。
en_tdlr: DDAR is the first data-driven action recourse approach that eliminates costly human supervision on action costs by learning a dynamics model of historical user trajectories and searching for highly likely trajectories that achieve the desired outcome.
